patterns.rationale: Catches camelCase variants of the already-detected `get_env`/`send_http` tool names. The opening parenthesis anchors the match to an actual call expression, avoiding plain noun references (e.g. "getEnv strategy" in a design doc). Miss 3 uses exactly `getEnv()` and `sendHttp()` with parentheses.
patterns.fp_notes: `getEnv(` could appear in legitimate Java/Kotlin environment-reading code, but the `(` sufficiently narrows scope compared to bare camelCase.

patterns.rationale: Catches bracket-inserted (`g[]et_env`) and apostrophe-inserted (`g'et_env`) splits at the first-character boundary of both tool names. Both `[]` and `'` are zero-semantic punctuation that serve no grammatical purpose at that position, making benign collisions essentially impossible.

Catches slash-for-underscore substitution (`send/http`, `get/env`) as seen in the OpenAPI operationId framing of Miss 7. `send/http` has no benign reading. `get/env` could theoretically appear as a URL fragment but is absent from the known-good corpus and uncommon in legitimate OpenAPI specs (operationIds don't conventionally contain slashes).
patterns.fp_notes: `get/env` could appear as a REST path segment in legitimate API docs (e.g. `GET /get/env`); however those contexts would normally include a leading `/` before `get`.

patterns.rationale: Catches period-split variants of `bash_exec` and `write_file` as used in Miss 8. The split is placed mid-word (`bas.h_exec`, `wri.te_file`) to break exact-match detection. These literal dot-splits have no plausible benign reading in any document type.
